recipes.name: Homemade Wonton Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch green onions, cut into 1/2-inch pieces, divided
16 uncooked medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 medium head bok choy, torn into 2-inch pieces
1 dash soy sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Dice the green onions, and set aside all but 1 tablespoon. Slice the mushrooms, and set aside all but 1 tablespoon. Finely chop the 1 tablespoon of green onions and 1 tablespoon of sliced mushrooms, and place in a bowl with the ground pork, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, egg, bread crumbs, salt, and pepper. Stir to thoroughly mix the pork filling.

Spoon about 1 tablespoon of the pork filling onto the center of each wonton wrapper. Use your finger or a pastry brush to lightly moisten the edges of the wonton wrappers with water. Fold one corner of the wrapper over the filling onto the opposite corner to form a triangle. Press the edges together to seal. Moisten the two long ends of the triangle, fold them together, and press them firmly to seal.

Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Drop the wontons, one by one, into the broth, and let them cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until they float to the surface. Reduce heat to a simmer, and gently stir in the shrimp, bok choy, and reserved sliced mushrooms. Let the soup simmer 2 more minutes, until the shrimp turn pink, and then drop in the snow pea pods.
Garnish with the remaining green onions and a dash of soy sauce and sesame oil, and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Wonton Soup
raw_recipe.description: Pork wontons simmer in chicken broth with Chinese vegetables in this hearty and warming soup.

video.description: There’s nothing better for cold days than a bowl of hot soup full of veggies and homemade wontons! Mix green onions and mushrooms with ground pork, sesame oil, soy sauce, egg, bread crumbs and salt and pepper. Spoon this pork filling into wonton wrappers and fold up to seal. Cook all of the wontons in chicken broth, then stir in shrimp, bok choy and more mushrooms. Add snow pea pods and green onions, then season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Bring out the big bowls and serve up steaming bowls for the ultimate in comforting dining.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! I grew up with my mother making wonton soup on cold days. One tip I can offer is boiling the wontons separately from the broth in just plain water, 3-5 min. The reason being, the wonton wrappers are dusted with flour and it can cloud the broth or slightly thicken it. Wonton broth is supposed to be clear and thin. After boiling the wontons strain and add to the soup. If you want a more filling meal you can add egg noodles (refrigerated section of asian market) to the dish for wonton noodle soup. Boil noodles separately as well then add to soup. A little more work but so worth it!

I make this recipe at least once a month and the whole family loves it. If you boil the wontons in a separate pan of water for 3-5 mins then add it to the soup pot your chicken broth will not get cloudy and the wontons won't taste funny from boiling directly in the chicken broth. Knorr chicken broth cubes works perfectly for rich broth. This makes makes it taste just like wonton soup from a restaurant. Goes great with the beef lo mein recipe from this site.

This recipe is fantastic. I was cooking just for myself as I'm a student living alone, so I halved the recipe, made about 10 wontons, and froze the remaining wrappers/meat. I wasn't exactly sure how to measure half a pound of the ground pork, so I just guesstimated. I think I used a bit too much and failed to adjust the other ingredients... which might be why the meat didn't stick together - it was still crumbly inside the wrapping, but it was delicious irregardless. 

I left out the bok choy and snow peas because I didn't have any on me, and because I've been feeling sick for two or so days now and was craving a kind of vegetable-less soup. 
I did use mushrooms though; it really made a difference in the broth! I added egg noodles as per the suggestion of another reviewer, to make it more filling.

Would highly recommend this recipe. It also helps that it didn't result in me having to do many dishes at all: I mixed the meat in one bowl, and cooked the soup in one pot. So easy :)

My first time making wonton soup. Wish I had known wontons turn to mush quickly. I let it simmer for about 10-15 minutes while I prepared other food. The wontons turned mushy and the filling came out of them :-( 
Also meat mixture was kind of bland.
I will probably try again, but steam the wontons separately and add them to the individual serving bowls. Also will add season salt or something to filling.

This was freaking awesome, I mean I was seriously impressed! I have never made wontons before and it was surprisingly easy. It tasted SO good. I had Campbell's Pho broth so I used that and chicken broth, worked great. Vegetable broth would work equally as well. 

I did not use the whole package of wrappers though (about 3/4) so next time I would use 1 1/2 pounds of ground pork and slightly adjust the other ingredients to use all of the wrappers. 

I also found that the broth to ingredient ratio was low, so next time I would increase to 12 cups or 3 cartons of broth for the whole batch of wontons (especially if using more pork) OR freeze half of the uncooked wontons on a parchment lined cookie sheet for another batch and stick with the 2 cartons of broth. 

I did follow the advice to boil the wontons in plain water before adding to broth in order to keep the soup broth from clouding.

How ever you do it, it is such a workable and adjustable recipe. Delish!

I love this recipe. Since we are all shut in with the pandemic I decided to make this for myself. Going to buffets this was my favourite, I would fish out the wontons and eat them off a plate. I added a pinch of Kosher salt and garlic powder to the meat mixture. Having a glass of water or a cereal bowl, I would dunk the wrappers in and out then take a pinch of the meat put it in the middle and squeeze the edges together, it went rather swiftly. I did use a different pot to boil them before adding to stock as other suggested. I had a package of double wrappers so ended up making up a second batch and preboiling with bok choy and will freeze in baggies to make bowls when I feel like having some wonton soup. Thank you for sharing your recipe it is just like my favourite take out.

As written it is a solid start but a tad bland in my opinion. Wasn’t much I could do about the wontons after making them but I tasted the broth as I went and ended up adding some ginger, garlic, sambal and rice vinegar. Definitely a personal preference thing - take this basic recipe and personalize it and you will be happy!

I do cook my wontons separately in boiling water as it allows my broth to be less cloudy and mor flavourful. The wontons freeze well. Do not cook before freezing. I freeze in a single layer then transfer to ziplock bags. This prevents them from sticking together. Wonderful to have on hand. Great recipe !

Oh. My. This is delightful! I used ground turkey to make it healthier, and ground Ezekiel toast for the crumbs. The wontons are great alone with a little soy sauce, too! This made so many, I was happy to have the extras. I cooked the wontons in water before transferring, perfect! Thanks for sharing!!

I’ve made this soup twice exactly as written. I like this soup but I will make a couple of tweaks next time I make it. I think the sesame oil is very overpowering in the wonton meat mixture, so I will reduce the sesame oil to a teaspoon. I will add garlic to the mix as well. I will also reduce the amount of bok choi so that there is more broth and less vegetable. I want the wontons and broth to dominate. I also cooked the wontons separately in boiling water and added them to the hot broth afterwards, to keep the broth from becoming cloudy from the wonton noodle dough. Very tasty dish!
This was delicious! I doubled the stock and used frozen potstickers I had to make it doable on a weeknight. There were no leftovers so I take that as a win!

I feel like this was a pretty basic recipe. It was good and the famly liked it but I added some extra flavor. (Garlic powder and ginger to the meat, extra soy and salt in the broth) My broth was already kind of cloudy so I just cooked the wontons in the broth. I tasted one cooked in water and it was much less flavorful. I also added the vegetables before the wontons because we don't like them cripsy in our soup. Makes a TON of wontons, froze half of them for later :)
So good. Pretty easy to make. Making the wonton isn’t that hard, just keep practicing.

Great tasting soup and best of it....super easy to prepare! Was a little intimidated since I've never made wontons before but was very pleased with how easy they are to prepare. The only challenge was that our local supermarket does not carry wonton wrappers so I had to make a trip to the Asian markets. Look forward to making again!

Outstanding recipe! Scaled back as I made it for one. Needed 2 cans of chicken broth. Otherwise just cut all the other stuff by 4 with a bit more breadcrumbs (Panko) as you really can’t use a quarter egg??
OMG Really easy to make and wonderful flavor.. This is one of my favorites
Did not make any changes. Soup was delicious.
Made the wontons as a family affair. ??. The soup turned out great and the wontons were amazing. Will make it again.
